title: smoke-scheduler-contracted-canary-orchestrator-with-linear-autocreate
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Adds a deterministic smoke-simulator and a contract-driven canary orchestrator. Enables automatic Linear ticket creation on rollback triggers. Non-breaking: opt-in feature behind rollout.experimental.canary_contracts flag.
description:
Motivation: We need predictable, auditable canary outcomes that are reproducible for postmortems and actionable when things go wrong. This PR introduces a small deterministic smoke-simulator and a "contracted canary" controller that evaluates canaries against user-defined contracts (latency, error-rate, model-confidence regressions). When a contract is violated the controller will automatically enact rollback policies and create a Linear incident (optionally tag and escalate) to reduce manual toil.

What this changes (summary): 1) A smoke-simulator service (tools/smoke-sim) that generates deterministic synthetic sessions matching customer session shapes; it seeds KV cache and simulates model/sidecar interactions. 2) A "canary contract" DSL (config/canary_contracts/{.yaml}) and parser that allows teams to express pass/fail gates (e.g. p95_latency < 220ms, top1_confidence_delta < -0.03, embedding_cosine_drop < 0.02). 3) A controller extension in services/rollout that evaluates live traffic and simulator probes against the contract, computes an explainable failure rationale (why a contract failed), and triggers rollback or graduated traffic adjustments. 4) Linear integration: when an auto-rollback occurs the controller creates a Linear issue with an attached failure summary and reproducible smoke-sim job spec; optionally includes links to replay artifacts stored in object storage. 5) Small CLI and runbook additions for SREs to run the smoke-sim locally and to replay failing sessions for bisect.

Checklist: - [x] smoke-simulator core and deterministic RNG seed support - [x] contract DSL + parser + schema validation - [x] controller integration + telemetry (telemetry includes contract_evaluations, contract_fail_reasons, simulator_match_rate) - [x] Linear autocreate + configurable escalation mapping - [x] Unit tests for parser and controller logic - [x] End-to-end integration test that spins a minimal controller + simulator in CI - [x] docs and quickstart example in redwood-quickstarts/canary-contracts

Backward compatibility and opt-in: This is non-breaking by default. Canary contracts are behind rollout.experimental.canary_contracts. Linear autocreate requires onboarding and API key configuration per org. Existing rollout behaviors are unchanged unless a contract is attached to a rollout resource.

Related Linear/Jira: ENG-11234 defines canonical contract semantics; SUP-4021 requested autocreate for expedited incident creation during customer-facing regressions. Also references design notes: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-11234/contracted-canary-design

Risk and mitigation: The simulator intentionally uses low load and well-scoped session shapes to avoid capacity interference. Controller has rate limits on automatic rollbacks and requires two independent contract failures in a 5-minute window (configurable) before a hard rollback. Autocreate has a dry-run mode for orgs to evaluate behavior without noise.

review_comments: Daniel Kim: Can you clarify the failure aggregation window? What if we see a short spike that triggers a rollback but stabilizes after one minute?

Aisha Patel: Response: controller requires two independent contract failures across the configured window (default 5m). Added unit tests for 1- and 2-failure scenarios and documented the window in docs/canary-contracts.md.
Mohamed El-Sayed: Linear autocreate looks powerful but noisy — can we add an org-level opt-out and a dry-run toggle?
Aisha Patel: Added dry-run mode and org-level enablement flag. Dry-run sends the same payload to the Linear endpoint but doesn't create issues; logs a simulated issue id for audit.
Priya Srinivasan: Please add a coupling test to ensure the smoke-sim workqueue does not starve production controllers under heavy test loads.

Aisha Patel: Added a concurrency-limited worker and a test harness that asserts production controllers remain within their memory budget. See tests/integration/canary_contracts/worker_throttle_test.go.
ci_checks: integration-e2e: passed (runs smoke-sim in CI sandbox)
bench: flaky on first run, reran and passed (adds ~15ms median to rollout path; deemed acceptable)
merge_outcome: Merged via squash-merge by Daniel Kim after two approvals. Squash commit message: 'contracted canary: add smoke-simulator, contract DSL, controller evaluation and Linear autocreate. ENG-11234'. Backported small schema changes to release/2026-02 for early adopter orgs.
notes: This PR is intended as an opt-in building block for teams that want automated, auditable canaries. Next steps: add a UI in the Console to author contracts and a scheduled job to run contracts against pinned historical traffic for regression detection.
